parties.counterparty: SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor)

plans.note: Liability language in this form is typically bundled with the all-caps disclaimer block (Article VIX and the WARRANTY DISCLAIMER text) or in GENERAL PROVISIONS. Check for a one-sided exclusion of consequential damages or a cap benefiting only Licensor, and for absence of carve-outs (confidentiality, IP infringement, willful misconduct).

No indemnity heading appears in the outline; scan GENERAL PROVISIONS, Article X and the disclaimer article for an embedded indemnity. If only a Licensee-gives indemnity exists, that is a deviation; if none exists at all, treat as missing (Vendor IP infringement indemnity expected in a software licence).

Article II (LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS) and the FIELD OF USE definition are the likely home of any restraint on Licensee's other businesses or use of competing platforms; also check Article VIII where the commercial terms sit.

The defined terms include 'Right of First Refusal', which strongly suggests an exclusivity-type constraint on Licensee's ability to source elsewhere; locate the operative ROFR text (likely Article VIII or Article II) and assess whether it forecloses alternative suppliers.

No MFN heading is evident; the tiered per-unit pricing schedule and Article VIII payment terms are the only plausible locations. Flag only if Licensee is required to extend best terms to Licensor — an MFN in our favour is not redlined.

Directly signposted: 'CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION' under Article X. Check mutuality, duration, scope (employees vs. customers/introducing brokers) and whether general advertising / unsolicited applicants are carved out.

Term/termination is not separately headed; the 'Initial Period' definition points to Article VIII or the later articles (XXIV / GENERAL PROVISIONS). Confirm Licensee has a notice-based exit without penalty and that Licensor cannot terminate at will mid-term.
Tied to the 'Initial Period' defined term; look for automatic extension language and the non-renewal notice window. A missing price-uplift cap is a rationale note, not a standalone deviation.

Expect governing law, venue and any arbitration clause in GENERAL PROVISIONS (Article XXIV). New York is likely given the 575 Madison Avenue addresses and would be compliant; flag only foreign law/foreign arbitration.

Assignment is a standard GENERAL PROVISIONS item; check for a consent requirement that blocks Licensee affiliate/successor transfers or gives Licensor a termination right on our change of control. The AFFILIATE definition is relevant.

Article II acknowledgements plus the DERIVATIVE WORK, MORAL RIGHTS, INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS and LICENSED TECHNOLOGY definitions. Watch for any assignment to Licensor of Licensee feedback, configurations, customer/trading data or derivative works.

Core grant in Article II, read with FIELD OF USE, LICENSED SOFTWARE, PLATFORM SOFTWARE and AFFILIATE. Test whether the grant is revocable at will, and whether affiliates and our contractors/introduced clients may use the Platform.

No audit heading appears; a usage/records audit right may be buried in Article II restrictions or in the volume-based billing terms (Market Day / Supplemental Payments reconciliation). If present, check notice, frequency, business hours and cost allocation.
Look in the payment/pricing provisions for penalty interest, shortfall charges or accelerated fees on early termination payable by Licensee. Service credits running to us are not flagged.

The document contains an express WARRANTY DISCLAIMER disclaiming merchantability, non-infringement and fitness, and stating errors may not be corrected — likely a full 'as is' with no performance warranty, which fails the fallback. Confirm no affirmative maintenance/service-level warranty exists elsewhere (maintenance obligations may sit in Article VIII).
No insurance heading in the outline; GENERAL PROVISIONS is the only plausible location. Given Licensor hosts the Platform and touches trading data, treat as missing if nothing is found.

Tiered per-ticket pricing (US$7.50 down to US$5.00) plus the 'Supplemental Payments' and 'Market Day' definitions suggest a volume-based minimum or take-or-pay. Verify whether a monthly minimum applies and whether Licensee has an exit if volumes are not met.

No wind-down or data-return heading is visible; check the termination consequences (wherever termination sits) and Article X confidentiality for a return/destruction obligation that might partially serve. Expect this to be missing and to require a transition assistance and data-return provision.
